name: @hdsp/connector
description: ZoeConnect Connector -- standalone Oracle Connector Windows Service ("ZoeConnect Connector 1.0 Deployment," 2026-07-22). Wraps @hdsp/oracle-client behind the Message Transport protocol so ZoeConnect's cloud backend (CloudOracleTransport) can talk to an on-prem Oracle HIS instance without a direct network path, and serves the versioned local REST API (/api/v1) + Connector Manager UI a hospital IT admin uses to activate, configure, and diagnose it. Bumped 0.1.0 -> 1.0.0 with the feature-freeze declared at the end of Task #103: activation, registration, JWT lifecycle, WebSocket transport, query-definition sync, the local API, the Manager UI, the system tray, Oracle configuration, and diagnostics are all considered feature-complete for this release; remaining work is packaging (Task #96), Windows validation, and hospital pilot, not new capabilities. See HDSP_CLOUD_CONNECTOR_ARCHITECTURE.md §18 for the versioning discipline this number is part of (Connector 1.0.0 / Connector Protocol v1 / local API v1, versioned independently).

pkg.//: ZoeConnect Connector 1.0 Deployment, Phase 1 (Packaging), 2026-07-22. Targets Windows x64 only -- this ships as a Windows Service; Linux/macOS targets aren't part of this product's distribution story. 'thin' mode node-oracledb is pure JS (no native addon), so no oracledb native binary needs special pkg asset handling -- if a hospital ever needs 'thick' mode, that requires a separately-installed Oracle Instant Client on the target machine regardless of how this binary is built, per @hdsp/oracle-client's own existing thick-mode handling (instantClientPath).
